definition: An architecture with many specialized sub-networks (experts) plus a router that activates only a few per input.
details: MoE layers keep a huge number of parameters but compute with only a small subset for each token, so they can scale parameter count without proportionally scaling per-token compute. The sparsely-gated approach demonstrated this at massive scale; today many frontier LLMs use MoE to combine large capacity with efficient inference.

explainer.lead: Mixture of Experts is an architecture with many specialised sub-networks plus a router that activates only a few per input. It matters because it scales parameter count without proportionally scaling per-token compute.

tiers.eli5: A big team of specialists, and a dispatcher sends each question only to the few experts best suited to answer it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use sparsely gated MoE layers to combine large capacity with efficient inference; a pitfall is router imbalance that leaves some experts undertrained.
tiers.paperLevel: MoE layers hold a huge number of parameters but compute with only a small subset per token via a router; the sparsely gated approach demonstrated this at massive scale.

explainer.example: A model could hold many expert sub-networks yet activate only a handful for each token, keeping per-token compute low while total parameters stay large.

citation.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
